_README: Per-camera speed calibration for speed_estimator.py.
A camera with an 'image_points' + 'world_points_m' pair gets ACCURATE speed
via a perspective transform (homography). A camera without it falls back to
a single 'fallback_ppm' (pixels per metre) - rough but stable.
HOW TO CALIBRATE A CAMERA (do this once per fixed camera):
1. Grab one clear frame from that camera.
2. Pick 4+ points on the FLAT ROAD surface that form a rectangle you can
measure in real life. Thailand motorway references:
- lane width  = 3.5 m
- dashed lane line = 3 m painted + 6 m gap (9 m pitch)
3. Read the pixel (x, y) of each point in the frame -> 'image_points'.
4. Write the same points in metres on a flat map (any origin) ->
'world_points_m', in the SAME order.
5. Add an entry below keyed by the camera id (e.g. 'TV73R', 'camera2').
Easiest way to build image_points + world_points_m: run
python scripts/calibrate_camera.py <camera_id> --image frame.jpg --rectangle --width 3.5 --length 27
and click the 4 road-rectangle corners; it writes the entry here for you.
Keys you may set per camera (all optional):
image_points      [[px,py], ...]  >=4, road-plane pixels
world_points_m    [[X,Y], ...]    same order, metres
fallback_ppm      number   used only if no homography (default 20)
max_speed_kmh     number   glitch clamp (default 160)
min_samples       integer  accepted updates before a speed shows (default 3)
stationary_mps    number   below this -> report 0 (default 0.6)
process_var       number   Kalman: how much velocity may drift (default 2.0)
measurement_var   number   Kalman: metre-measurement noise; raise=smoother/laggier (default 1.5)
gate_chi2         number   reject a reading beyond this Mahalanobis dist (default 13.8)
point_median      integer  frames of median smoothing on the tracked pixel (default 3)
window_seconds    number   displacement cross-check window (default 1.0)
max_accel_mps2    number   cap on how fast the label may change (default 6.0)
conv_var          number   filter must converge below this before reporting (default 20.0)

BACKFILL NOTE (2026-09-22): image_width/image_height added to every camera below that already had image_points, all set to 1280x720 - confirmed via ffprobe that every camera in src/cameras.js streams natively at 1280x720, and that resolution is what both the manual-click UI and auto_calibrate_vp.py were actually operating in when these points were recorded. Before this, speed_estimator.py applied these native-resolution points directly to ~640px inference-frame pixels with no rescaling - off by roughly 10x (not a clean 2x, since a homography does not scale linearly), which is why speed readings had been so erratic. New calibrations (from either tool) now record their own resolution automatically.
